result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.

result.rule: When the description states that several activities are all required before a later activity or outcome: Model the activities as parallel branches and synchronize all branches with a parallel gateway before the later activity or outcome.

When the description says an additional activity may be performed before a later activity that follows regardless: Model the additional activity as a distinct optional path that rejoins the main flow before the later shared activity.

When the description says an activity may or may not occur before a later required activity: model the optional activity as one branch of an exclusive gateway, and merge the branches before the later required activity

When the description explicitly orders activities or says that work continues until a stated condition is reached: Model the activities in the stated sequence, and do not represent them as parallel or mutually exclusive branches unless the description explicitly supports concurrency or a decision.

result.rule: Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Create reusable bpmn:message elements and messageRef only when communication content or shared message identity matters.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.

result.rule: When the description distinguishes an event or activity by its action, actor, object, recipient, or another meaningful qualifier: Label each BPMN element so that it preserves those stated details without substituting a broader or different meaning.
When the description specifies an activity’s object, recipient, or other meaningful qualifier: Preserve that qualifier in the BPMN task label rather than replacing it with a broader paraphrase.

When the description distinguishes a process trigger, an activity, or an outcome from other stages of the process: Label each BPMN element according to the meaning of its corresponding described trigger, activity, or outcome; do not substitute a different stage or its purpose or result.

When the description says that a participant performs an action that initiates the process: Model the process trigger with a start event, then model the participant’s described action as a distinct task; do not use the action itself as the start event.
